items.extracted_title: NVIDIA, Microsoft Kick Off a New Beginning for Windows PCs With RTX Spark and AI Agents
items.extracted_excerpt: NVIDIA RTX Spark pre-orders open October 16, and DGX Station for Windows brings GB300 AI infrastructure to the enterprise desktop.
items.extracted_text_for_analysis: At a Microsoft event in San Francisco on Wednesday, Jensen Huang and Satya Nadella outlined how NVIDIA and Microsoft are co-engineering hardware and software for AI agents to run on Windows PCs. NVIDIA was founded because of Windows, Huang said. Now AI agents are coming to Windows. “If you look at the entire journey of our company, Windows was at the core of it,” Huang said, tracing back NVIDIA’s support for Windows and Microsoft over several decades. “If not for Windows there would be no GeForce.” NVIDIA founder and CEO Jensen Huang connected that history — and his long-term vision — to the agentic era Wednesday during a fireside chat with Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella hosted by Sriram Krishnan, a former senior White House policy advisor on AI at the Windows AI and Surface event, held at Dogpatch Studios in San Francisco. “The thing that I really give Jensen all the credit for, quite frankly, is that consistency of vision of what this can be—not today, not tomorrow, but as a secular trend,” Nadella said. “And that’s what brings us to this moment.” “The personal computer is the ultimate tool, it’s my ultimate tool, and for a whole generation of people, it’s our ultimate tool,” Huang said. “What happens in the era of agents, when the agent is on your computer? It is now your personal assistant.” The event opened with Nadella before Pavan Davuluri, Microsoft’s EVP of Windows and Devices, walked through the Windows updates designed for the agentic era. Turning Windows into a secure platform for agents, Microsoft announced general availability of Microsoft Execution Containers (MXC), the OS-level infrastructure that lets agents run safely and persistently in the background, under operating system control. “We are building these primitives directly into Windows, so agents can be secured, observed and governed,” Davuluri explained. “With MXC, Microsoft Security, and Agent 365, we’re unlocking the full potential of agents on Windows.” Nadella returned to that theme in his talk with Huang. “We needed to make the desktop the most secure place for agents to execute,” Nadella said. “What Satya just said is going to be the foundation of the next generation of IT as we know it,” Huang said. “Just as Windows and DirectX revolutionized how applications were built, MXC is going to revolutionize how agents are built and deployed.” A New Beginning for Windows PCs: Preorder RTX Spark Laptops Today Among the announcements Huang and Nadella outlined Wednesday, RTX Spark puts the full NVIDIA AI stack into Windows laptops and compact desktops, with laptop preorders open today and available October 16. Compact desktops will be available for sale in November. Windows is bringing local AI closer to everyday work, while new hardware gives developers room to run increasingly capable models right on their PC. Introducing Surface Laptop Ultra, Pavan Davuluri tied that vision to NVIDIA RTX Spark. “We built Surface Laptop Ultra around NVIDIA RTX Spark. With up to 128 gigs of unified memory and up to a petaflop of AI compute, you can run models on this laptop that simply don’t fit on a traditional machine,” Davuluri said. Systems are coming from Acer, ASUS, Dell, HP, Lenovo, Microsoft, MSI and Gigabyte with designs ranging from slim laptops to compact desktops built for always-on agents. RTX Spark combines an NVIDIA Blackwell RTX GPU with up to 6,144 cores, and an up to 20-core NVIDIA Grace CPU connected at 600 GB/s. One petaflop of FP4 AI performance and up to 128GB unified memory makes RTX Spark effective for local AI. It can run models such as Qwen 3.8 Flash Next, a 125B model with 51B n-gram that matches the intelligence of many cloud models, unmetered and without sending data to the cloud. RTX Spark runs the full NVIDIA CUDA platform — the same software stack that runs across NVIDIA hardware — and is built for every way people use a PC: - Developers can move models, tools and workflows without rewriting, running the same NVIDIA AI stack from RTX Spark to DGX Station. - Creators get 5th-generation Tensor Cores with NVFP4 support, hardware-accelerated AV1, and 4:2:2 video encode and decode, DLSS and RTX ray tracing across the full production pipeline. - Gamers can run AAA games at 1440p over 100 frames per second with DLSS 5, Reflex and G-SYNC. The compact desktop configuration puts the same RTX Spark superchip in a small chassis designed for 24/7 operation — a dedicated local AI system that keeps agents running continuously. Preorder RTX Spark today. NVIDIA DGX Station for Windows: Frontier AI Compute on the Enterprise Desktop The event previewed NVIDIA DGX Station for Windows today — the first deskside AI supercomputer to bring GB300 Grace Blackwell-class AI infrastructure directly into the Windows ecosystem. “This unlocks the power to run frontier-class models locally,” Davuluri said. “Capabilities that once required renting a cluster, now in a deskside supercomputer.” Until now, DGX Station ran on Linux — which meant enterprise developers maintained two separate environments: Linux for heavy AI workloads and Windows for the productivity tools, applications and workflows. The vast majority of Fortune 500 companies are standardized on Windows, and that gap has cost developers time and resources — developers either moved to Linux to access AI compute, or stayed in Windows with limited hardware options for heavy-duty model development and multi-agent workloads. NVIDIA DGX Station for Windows runs on the GB300 Grace Blackwell Ultra Desktop Superchip, delivering 748GB of coherent memory and up to 20 petaFLOPS of FP4 AI compute — enough to run models up to a trillion-parameter scale locally. Teams of developers and researchers at AI-native companies, leading research labs and enterprises can build and run always-on AI agents that connect directly to the Windows applications and infrastructure they already use, and fine-tune and inference large models without leaving their primary machine. Linux AI toolchains remain accessible through WSL when needed. Learn more about NVIDIA DGX Station for Windows and sign up to be the first to know when it’s available. Follow NVIDIA RTX Spark on X, Instagram, TikTok and Facebook — and stay informed by subscribing to the NVIDIA Local AI newsletter. Follow NVIDIA Workstation on LinkedIn and X. See notice regarding software product information.

items.extracted_excerpt: College Planner is coming to ChatGPT for Teens to help students manage college applications, alongside new flashcards, quizzes, and a teen AI council.
items.extracted_text_for_analysis: Since we introduced ChatGPT for Teens—the default experience automatically applied to accounts identified as under 18—we’ve seen young people use it to learn, explore ideas and solve everyday problems. Today, we’re sharing early progress on ChatGPT for Teens, including how teens are using its learning tools, along with new ways for teens to study and prepare for college. ChatGPT’s 1.2 billion users span many countries, communities and backgrounds. That reach makes it especially important to build tools that help young people with different resources and opportunities learn and prepare for their futures. ChatGPT for Teens is designed to help young people learn, think critically and deepen their understanding. As ChatGPT for Teens became available to more teens globally, those with access sent about 2.7 million more learning-related messages on average than those who didn’t have it yet. Once enrolled, teens use ChatGPT for Teens’ learning tools at scale. The most selected conversation starter prompts are “ask questions to develop my ideas,” “give feedback on my draft,” and “help me check my evidence.” In one week, nearly 1.2 million teens used Learning Visualizations to better understand math and science concepts, and more than 180,000 used Study Mode for step-by-step learning support. ChatGPT for Teens includes built-in reminders to encourage teens to take breaks. On average, teens spend under 15 minutes a day on ChatGPT. While less than 2% of teens spend more than three consecutive hours on ChatGPT, in almost half of teen conversations with a break reminder, teens took a break or ended their conversation within five minutes. These usage patterns remain well below the publicly reported(opens in a new window) average of 5 hours for teen social media usage, and reflect a different kind of experience: ChatGPT is designed for learning, building, and creativity, rather than passive scrolling. Among teens with sessions longer than three consecutive hours, over 80% had at least one prompt related to learning. These early signs are encouraging and we’ll continue to evaluate the experience and learn from teens, families and educators to improve ChatGPT for Teens. Hundreds of thousands of US teens use ChatGPT each week to plan for college. They’re using it to plan applications, track deadlines, research schools and understand financial aid. That’s why we’ll soon be adding College Planner to ChatGPT for Teens. We’re designing it to help students manage the practical steps of applying to college, without taking over the personal work of figuring out where they want to apply. Students have different levels of access to support with college applications. Our goal is to make help more accessible, regardless of financial circumstances, alongside guidance from counselors, advisers, and families. College Planner brings together application requirements, deadlines, tasks, and financial-aid steps for schools on a student’s list in one plan. Students applying to several colleges can return to it to update their progress, use the timeline to plan ahead and see what’s left to do. They can also ask ChatGPT questions along the way, from what a requirement means to how to get started. By bringing these steps together, we aim to save students and families time and make a stressful process feel more manageable. We’re designing the initial US experience for high-school students in grades 10–12 who are planning to attend a four-year college. We plan to bring College Planner to students in more countries and expand support to two-year colleges, technical colleges, trade schools and more over time. College Planner also helps students figure out how to pay for college. They can get help understanding financial aid requirements, track each school’s aid deadlines, and explore scholarships and fee waivers. Keeping track of an application is only one part of preparing for college. Many students also need someone to help them make sense of their options. Alongside College Planner, we’re supporting College Advising Corps(opens in a new window), a nonprofit that places recent college graduates as advisers in under-resourced high schools to help students navigate the path to higher education. OpenAI’s contribution will help the organization expand into new states and create an AI fellowship program. Through the fellowship, advisers across participating states will test and share practical ways to use AI to help more students navigate the path to college. AI can help students manage application and enrollment tasks. Advisers can help them consider their options and decide what to do next. When we introduced ChatGPT for Teens, we committed to keep improving the experience. We’re supporting Boston Children’s Hospital’s Digital Wellness Lab(opens in a new window) and its independent Student Advisory Council(opens in a new window) over the next three years to learn directly from young people about how AI fits into their lives and to give teenagers a meaningful stake at the table as AI is being designed. For the 2026–27 school year, the Lab will bring together ~22 students across two tracks: ~12 students ages 14–18 working on digital wellbeing projects in their communities and ~10 students ages 16–20, focused on building AI chatbots and emerging technology. These students will work alongside researchers and clinicians on digital wellbeing and AI projects. Students in the AI track will test tools and recommend changes based on how they use AI in learning and their personal lives. We expect to seek feedback on teen safety defaults, parental controls and notifications and AI literacy. Teens should play a central role in developing the tools that will shape their future. Teens will test tools and develop recommendations for the people building them. Our aim is to bring those recommendations into product and model decisions early and to report back to students on what we change and why. This advisory board will give them a direct voice in that work and share their insights and recommendations to help the wider industry build better tools for young people. We heard from students that photographing and uploading their notes to ChatGPT can take hours. We’re making it easier for students to turn their notes into study materials like flashcards and quizzes. With continuous, multi-photo capture, students can photograph multiple pages of notes and automatically combine them into a single PDF, ready to upload to ChatGPT. This is available on iOS, and we’re working to bring it to Android. We’re also adding flashcards to help teens practice what they’re learning. A student preparing for a biology test, for example, can upload class notes or choose a topic, and ChatGPT can turn the material into cards to review. They can mark the cards they know, return to the ones they missed or shuffle the deck for another round. Decks are saved in a teen’s Library, so it’s easy to pick up where they left off. items.extracted_title: Radisson Hotel Group brings hotel discovery into ChatGPT
items.extracted_excerpt: Radisson partnered with Accenture to build a ChatGPT plugin using OpenAI technology, helping travelers find, compare, and book hotels while planning their trips.
items.extracted_text_for_analysis: Radisson Hotel Group brings hotel discovery into ChatGPT Radisson partnered with Accenture to build a ChatGPT plugin using OpenAI technology, helping travelers find, compare, and book hotels while planning their trips. Booking conversion ~1.5× Early plugin conversion versus organic search (Jul–Aug 2026) Sponsored ads 54% Of recorded checkout and booking events attributed to ad views Delivery speed 6 Weeks to build and launch the ChatGPT plugin Travelers increasingly turn to AI to decide where to stay, often shortlisting hotels or building an entire itinerary before they ever visit a hotel website. Through its partnership with Accenture Song, Radisson Hotel Group is using OpenAI technology to reach guests earlier in that planning journey. The Radisson Hotels ChatGPT plugin(opens in a new window) helps travelers compare hotels and explore travel options through an interactive experience, and early results show booking conversion approximately 1.5 times that of Radisson’s organic search. Alongside the plugin, Radisson is among the hospitality pioneers running sponsored advertising in ChatGPT(opens in a new window), bringing its branded plugin and paid advertising together as part of an integrated discovery strategy. Radisson Hotel Group brings together ten distinctive hotel brands across EMEA and APAC, with more than 1,640 hotels in operation and under development. For the past seven years, Accenture has helped Radisson grow bookings through its direct digital channel, combining digital media strategy and execution with a transformation roadmap for its core digital capabilities. A stronger direct digital channel helps Radisson attract guests more efficiently and build relationships that encourage repeat stays. For hotel owners, this translates into stronger commercial performance and greater long-term value from their partnership with Radisson Hotel Group. This work meant Accenture had a front-row seat to AI’s transformative impact on the travel industry. “Almost overnight, there was a new surface where prospects were getting inspired, comparing different alternatives, and almost making their decision before even reaching a hotel’s website,” explains Borja Lizarraga Rodríguez, Data & AI Lead at Accenture Song. “It was critical for us to ensure the visibility of Radisson across this new experience.” As an Elite Partner of the OpenAI Partner Network, Accenture collaborated with OpenAI to explore strategies for organic positioning in ChatGPT. From these conversations, Accenture developed the idea of a ChatGPT plugin(opens in a new window): “We wanted to bring the value proposition of Radisson into ChatGPT and make it extremely user-friendly, ensuring things like maps, hotel details, and prices were integrated in the simplest way,” says Lizarraga. With the help of agentic development, the team built and launched the Radisson Hotels plugin(opens in a new window) in just six weeks. It lets users see Radisson Hotel suggestions on a map, compare pricing, and view hotel amenities in detail directly in ChatGPT, then continue to the Radisson site to complete their booking. Early results from the Radisson Hotels plugin in ChatGPT show a visit-to-booking conversion rate approximately 1.5 times Radisson’s organic search for July–August 2026. The plugin gives travelers a direct path from conversational hotel discovery to Radisson’s own booking channel. A recent ChatGPT update means users no longer have to type @RadissonHotels before their query; if they have the plugin installed, ChatGPT will automatically show it whenever relevant. “If you’re planning a trip to Madrid, and there’s a new Radisson Hotel you might want to consider, now in ChatGPT it will just automatically work,” says Brittny Cantor, Agentic Commerce Lead at Accenture. “We’re really excited about that change to increase discoverability.” The plugin gives Radisson a new way to reach travelers organically in ChatGPT. Radisson is also among the hospitality pioneers launching sponsored advertising campaigns in ChatGPT as part of an integrated discovery strategy. Since launching in July, its campaigns have expanded into additional markets across Europe and beyond. More than half of the campaign’s recorded checkout and booking events were attributed through view-through measurement, extending Radisson’s assessment of discovery beyond direct ad clicks. Accenture designed the underlying infrastructure to support more than a single application. The MCP server and APIs that Accenture developed for the Radisson plugin are also powering the ads experience and will play a role in other new features to come. Radisson is aware that with AI, the way users make decisions about travel has changed dramatically and will continue to evolve. They’re determined to be the first among their competitors to capitalize on these changes, becoming not only a hotel chain but an advisor on the entire travel experience. Its next priorities include encouraging plugin adoption and developing additional functionality within the ChatGPT experience. “What stands out about Radisson is its ability to move quickly while keeping a clear focus on guests and hotel owners. Together, we are applying new technology where it can make a meaningful difference: helping travelers find the right hotel, strengthening direct guest relationships, and supporting more profitable growth,” Borja Lizarraga says. “Great stays have always started with good advice. Today, more of that advice happens in conversation, and we moved quickly to be there. Initial results are encouraging, with our ChatGPT plugin converting at around 1.5 times organic search. This is just the start: wherever a journey begins, we want Radisson to be the advisor guests trust and the direct channel that delivers lasting value for our hotels and owners,” says Velit Dundar, Vice President, Global Ecommerce, Radisson Hotel Group.

items.title: GPT-6 and Intelligent UI for everyone
items.title_original: GPT-6 and Intelligent UI for everyone
items.title_en: GPT-6 and Intelligent UI for everyone
items.summary_zh: OpenAI 更新了模型或产品能力更新，关键在于模型能力、部署成本、权限控制或开发者工作流的实际变化。
items.summary_en: GPT‑6 is rolling out globally in ChatGPT with Intelligent UI, delivering faster responses with visuals and interactive experiences you can explore and use directly.
items.extracted_title: GPT-6 and Intelligent UI for everyone
items.extracted_excerpt: GPT‑6 is rolling out globally in ChatGPT with Intelligent UI, delivering faster responses with visuals and interactive experiences you can explore and use directly.
items.extracted_text_for_analysis: Last month we introduced the first GPT‑6 models for paid customers and today we're bringing that next generation of intelligence to more people with a new GPT‑6 model built for more than 1.2 billion people who use ChatGPT each week. GPT‑6 in ChatGPT introduces Intelligent UI, a new capability that allows ChatGPT to answer quickly with fully interactive user interfaces that make everyday answers more visual, make learning complex topics easier and that can quickly create a tool to solve a task right in the moment. We’ve trained GPT‑6 to compose responses using text, visuals and interactive elements, choosing how they fit together based on your question. With Intelligent UI, responses can include graphics, tappable buttons, forms, charts, and interactive experiences you can use directly in your conversation. The format depends on what you’re asking. A comparison might work best side by side. An explanation might be easier to understand through an interactive diagram. And when a simple text answer is the most useful response, ChatGPT can give you that. ChatGPT can make a plan easier to follow by showing how it fits together. The timing for a Sunday roast can sit alongside the recipe, or the stops on a road trip can appear on a map, with notes on what’s worth a detour. Visual and interactive explanations let you explore how something works, change an input to see what happens, or work through a problem step by step. You can also ask ChatGPT to create a tool for the task at hand, such as a calculator to explore how savings could grow, a bill splitter for dinner with friends, or a game you can play in the conversation. With Intelligent UI, we gave GPT‑6 the freedom to create the most useful interface for each question, while keeping the experience fast and familiar across web and mobile. We built a library of native, streamable components, along with a compiler that processes the interface as the model generates it. The library gives each response a familiar design foundation while leaving the model room to decide how the pieces fit together. The compiler allows the interface to appear progressively as the model generates it, without waiting for the entire response to be complete. We expanded our training methods to help the model make thoughtful decisions about content, layout, visuals, and interaction. This included evaluating the interfaces it creates for clarity, usefulness, and completeness. GPT‑6 learned to use the component library and make good design decisions, including how to organize information clearly, when to use interactivity, and when a simple text response is enough. There's still work ahead to improve the model's design judgment and expand what it can create, but Intelligent UI marks a significant shift in how people interact with ChatGPT. Instead of fitting every question into the same conversational format, ChatGPT can combine UI, data, and actions to create entirely new ways for people to explore, understand, and interact with information. With GPT‑6, we’re also making it possible for ChatGPT to begin answering while it continues to think. With the introduction of reasoning models, users could get help with much harder problems, but had to wait for the model to finish thinking before getting an answer. Now, ChatGPT can interleave thinking with answering. We trained it to take into account the user’s waiting time and progressively compose an answer using its knowledge and findings up to that point. It learned to build answers across multiple partial responses, each adding useful information without unnecessary filler, while keeping the full answer as cohesive and factual as one written all at once. In an internal evaluation of high-value, everyday agentic tasks, GPT‑6 Extra High is able to begin answering in the same amount of time as GPT‑5.6 Medium while achieving a better overall score than GPT‑5.6 Extra High. For questions that need web search, GPT‑6 Instant starts answering 44% sooner, on average, than GPT‑5.6 Instant. GPT‑6 also improves the quality of answers that require web search. It makes better decisions about when to look something up and more reliably finds information that supports its answer. In an internal evaluation of difficult problems, GPT‑6 correctly addressed the key aspect of the user’s question more often than GPT‑5.6. As we bring more intelligent AI to more people, we work to improve how it recognizes real-world risks, how honestly it responds, and how well it respects the limits that people set. GPT‑6 makes progress in each of these areas, building on several of Astra’s safety advances to better resist attempts to bypass its safety training, follow safeguards, and be clearer about what it can and can’t do relative to GPT‑5.6 Sol. We updated its safety training based on lessons from real-world use to strengthen protections against high-risk misuse involving cyberattacks, biological threats, and violence. In adversarial testing, GPT‑6 showed stronger resistance to attempts to bypass its safety training, particularly attacks that adapt across multiple turns. GPT‑6 is also trained to respond safely in higher-risk scenarios while avoiding unnecessary refusals of harmless requests. This includes using conversation history and relevant context to recognize risks that may not be apparent from a single prompt. We ran alignment evaluations throughout training, assessing honesty and responses to safety restrictions. GPT‑6 is better at recognizing and communicating the limits of its own capabilities, including when it lacks the information or tools needed to answer. More detail on the results and our review is available in the system card(opens in a new window). GPT‑6 with Intelligent UI starts rolling out globally to ChatGPT Plus, Pro, Business and Enterprise tiers today in the Chat tab. Starting tomorrow, the rollout expands to Free and Go tiers. Enterprise availability depends on workplace admin settings. GPT‑6 in ChatGPT is powered by GPT‑6 Sol for Plus, Pro, Business, and Enterprise tiers, and GPT‑6 Luna for Free and Go tiers. Both are tuned for everyday conversation. This update applies to the Chat experience in ChatGPT. The models powering Work and Codex are not changing as part of this release. Our mission is to deliver the benefits of artificial general intelligence safely to all of humanity. GPT‑6 brings our latest advances in intelligence to the more than 1.2 billion people who use ChatGPT every week. Intelligent UI is a step toward a ChatGPT that can shape an interface around what you’re trying to do. Over time, we want ChatGPT to create more of the interfaces people need for everyday tasks. You should be able to describe what you want to accomplish and work with an experience built around it. For decades, people have had to learn how to use software, navigating fixed interfaces designed around particular tasks. We believe the future will be different. Instead of people adapting to software, software will adapt to people.

items.extracted_title: OpenAI Decisions API now available on AI Gateway - Vercel
items.extracted_excerpt: Vercel AI Gateway now supports OpenAI's Decisions API, with GPT-6 Luna Decisions and other decision models through the OpenAI SDK, AI SDK, and AI CLI
items.extracted_text_for_analysis: OpenAI's Decisions API is now available on AI Gateway through an OpenAI-compatible /v1/decisions endpoint. Use it with GPT-6 Luna Decisions or any other decision model on AI Gateway. Decision models answer typed questions about a shared input and return probabilities, choices, and scores instead of generated text, which suits routing, triage, guardrails, and rubric scoring. You can ask predicate (yes/no), choice, and score questions against the same input in one request. openai/gpt-6-luna-decisions is a separate model ID from openai/gpt-6-luna, which stays a language model for text generation. Requests to the decisions ID go to the Decisions API and are billed at its rates. Call it with the OpenAI SDK, the AI SDK, the existing HTTP API at /v1/evaluate, or the AI CLI. Copy link to headingUpgrading decisions.create requires the OpenAI SDK 7.30.0 or later for JavaScript, or 3.26.0 or later for Python. In the AI SDK, experimental_decide requires ai 7.0.128 or later. Copy link to headingOpenAI SDK and AI SDK Point the OpenAI SDK at AI Gateway and call decisions.create as you would against OpenAI. In the AI SDK, questions are keyed by name and the yes/no type is called boolean. Each key in questions becomes a key in answers: import OpenAI from 'openai'; const openai = new OpenAI({ apiKey: process.env.AI_GATEWAY_API_KEY, baseURL: 'https://ai-gateway.vercel.sh/v1',}); const decision = await openai.decisions.create({ model: 'openai/gpt-6-luna-decisions', input: 'I was charged twice. Please refund me.', questions: [ { type: 'choice', name: 'department', instructions: 'Which team should handle this?', choices: [ { value: 'billing', description: 'Charges and refunds' }, { value: 'technical', description: 'Bugs and outages' }, ], }, ],}); console.log(decision.answers); Answers come back as an array in question order, each carrying the question's name. Set model to any decision model, including Jev, Liquid d1, and Laya. See the OpenAI-compatible Decisions API reference for request limits and error formats, the decision documentation for the AI SDK, or browse all decision models on AI Gateway.

items.extracted_title: Claude Haiku 5.5 now available on AI Gateway - Vercel
items.extracted_excerpt: Call Claude Haiku 5.5 through Vercel AI Gateway with one API key: no provider account, automatic fallbacks, spend tracking, and traces on every request.
items.extracted_text_for_analysis: Claude Haiku 5.5 from Anthropic is now available on AI Gateway. It is built for high-volume, cost-sensitive tasks such as summaries, context compaction, database queries, and classification, and works as a subagent alongside larger Claude models on coding work. It is also the fastest Claude model at standard speed, which suits live customer support and browser use. Test it as a direct upgrade wherever you use Claude Haiku 4.5 today. Haiku 5.5 is the first Haiku model with effort levels. It uses adaptive thinking and supports low, medium, high, xhigh, and max effort, which set how much the model thinks and how many tokens it uses. You can turn thinking off at low, medium, and high. At xhigh and max, thinking must stay on. Haiku 5.5 supports Zero Data Retention on AI Gateway. It ships with biology and cybersecurity safeguards, so it may decline some requests in those areas. Call it through the AI SDK, the Chat Completions, Responses, and Anthropic Messages APIs, or a coding agent connected to AI Gateway. Set effort with reasoning in the AI SDK or reasoning_effort in Chat Completions. Use anthropic/claude-haiku-5.5 as the model name: import { streamText } from 'ai'; const result = streamText({ model: 'anthropic/claude-haiku-5.5', reasoning: 'low', prompt: 'Extract the city and date from: Meet me in Paris on May 3.',}); To use it in Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, and more, install the latest Vercel CLI and run setup: npm i -g vercel@latestvercel ai-gateway setup Then select anthropic/claude-haiku-5.5 in the agent. See the coding agents guide for details. Try Claude Haiku 5.5 in the model playground. AI Gateway provides a unified API for calling models, tracking usage and cost, and configuring retries, failover, and performance optimizations for higher-than-provider uptime. It includes built-in custom reporting, Zero Data Retention support, budgets for API keys, routing rules, and more. AI Gateway reflects provider pricing with no markup and does not charge a platform fee on inference, including on Bring Your Own Key (BYOK) requests. You can view all language models available on AI Gateway.
